item.title: Festive Jello Strikes Back
item.description: A predatory cognitohazard visually perceived as a plate of Christmas jello.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery, Horror

Elevator Pitch: A seemingly innocent plate of Christmas gelatin (Festive season!), through further analysis, has been determined to be a cognitohazard employed by a gelatinous anomaly. It is able to detect prey by secreting pheromones into the air that when inhaled, awakens a predatory instinct within the gelatinous mass to envelop and consume affected prey item within a 5-meter radius of the plate.

Central Narrative: Field Agents dispatched to investigate an unexplained suburban disappearance of an entire family fails to report to Command. Ergo, an MTF team is deployed to follow up the disappearance, discovering human remains contained inside a mass of layered Christmas jello of an unknown origin. The object is retrieved and returned to an SCP Site wherein it is contained and the Foundation proceeds to conduct testing on the anomaly and gain additional understanding of its anomalous properties for optimal containment procedures.

After the SCP is confirmed a cognitohazard, it is suspected that the SCP was manufactured by a hitherto unknown Group of Interest. The Foundation launches a wider investigation into the origin of the SCP, sending Field Agents to return to the abandoned suburban home where it was originally discovered. The exploration log indicates that the agent discovers the original packaging and after finding out the brand name, another subsequent investigation reveals the identity of the Group of Interest that managed to evade Foundation radar up to this incident. The story ends with a footnote that ongoing surveillance and monitoring of the G.O.I is underway in order to assess the threat level of the parent G.O.I and ultimately deem whether Foundation intervention is necessary.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook starts with the mysterious disappearance of Foundation Field Agents in a peaceful suburban area with no record of kidnapping, homicides or break and entry crimes. This leads to the discovery of the SCP (Through an exploration log). Then the SCP Foundation attempts to understand the SCP's unknown properties (Experimentation log), allowing effective containment to be achieved. The SCP Foundation reasons from its nature as a cognitohazard that there was a strong possibility that the SCP was artificially engineered. The audience is constantly kept engaged by a linear narrative starting off with mystery that later unfolds into a deeper investigation of the SCP's origins.

Additional Notes: Have yet to determine a name for the G.O.I responsible for the manufacturing of the SCP, and have not yet decided whether the G.O.I are a belligerent or benevolent organisation.

item.title: June the 31st
item.description: The Day No One Remembers.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): ACS

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is both the day of June the 31st and the global event that occurs on that day. During the day, members of the public appear to be in a state of complete wholeness and engage in unorthodox, but not unnatural activities. These activities can range from having a picnic in the park, gardening, napping in a graveyard to hugging and weeping. Knowledge of the day appears to be instinctive. People seem to remember it the moment the day begins and steadily forget about it when it finishes1. It also appears that those working for or associated with the Foundation are exempt from this event and are able to remember the happenings of the day. They also don't feel the state of wholeness that the general public experience on the day.

Central Narrative: Something is in the air. Like an uncanny calm. Almost as if the whole world had sighed with relief and tranquility.

The overall story of this SCP is the strange, tranquil state the world enters on June the 31st, the day no-one will remember. Throughout the day, people enter a mindset they will rarely enter on any other day. Everyone is truly occupying their lives. That is, everyone except those in the Foundation, as they appear to be exempt from the SCP's effect. This is further emphasised when Foundation researchers interview people during the SCP. The interviewee treats foundation staff with slight pity and compassion, as if the Foundation is a child who doesn't understand something.

It's suggested that the SCP is necessary in some way. During one experiment, people were subjected to a strong narcotic and skipped the day entirely. Upon waking up, the subject appeared distant, mournful and depressive and continued in this state throughout their lives. It would appear that this SCP maintains a kind of wellbeing inside humanity.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: What I'm really trying to get across is both a feeling of calm peace experienced by the public and a sort of sad envy and exclusion experienced by the Foundation Staff. I haven't seen an SCP which does something beautiful and emphasises the loss Foundation Staff experience when they join the Foundation.

Footnotes
1. This is demonstrated through interviews and experiments.

item.title: Roland The Headless Thompson Gunner
item.description: Yes, inspired by the Warren Zevon song.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Character-Driven, Weird, Action

Elevator Pitch: Tales of vengeance-seeking headless specters have been around for awhile, but there's one that goes underappreciated: Roland the Headless Thompson Gunner, from the song of the same name by Warren Zevon. It seemed like the perfect fuel for an SCP, especially combined with my affinity for weird, character-driven stories.

Central Narrative: The headless spirit of a betrayed mercenary from the first Congo war still roams the earth, seeking out his killer. All the while the Foundation attempts to track him down and put a lock on him as he gets closer to his goal, told through incident logs. Eventually the Foundation finds Roland's killer and brings him in, only for Roland to eventually get in and put an end to him, after which he "shuts down", so the Foundation can easily cram him in a room.
Time passes with the headless gunner just standing there motionless, with several attempts being made to speak to him and see if he's at all aware of his dead state (to no response). Things stay like this until several undercover Chaos Insurgency agents make their move, turning against their Foundation "co-workers". However, even if he couldn't respond, Roland still heard those sessions, and it got him thinking. The being that once fought for money, then for his own revenge, has been awakened again by the cruel betrayal happening in close proximity, and now shall fight for others. One last action scene/log, before Roland vanishes off into the night, his muzzle-flashes illuminating traitor's deeds all around the world.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Roland's killer is initially listed as a POI, and right off the bat in conprocs personnel are advised to immediately report any possible information or leads on who he is, to stop the anomaly's manifestations. From there the procedures list out the types of places prone to getting Roland'ed and weaves a tale of a maniacal globetrotting chase across the seedy underbelly of the world.

Additional Notes: The original song can be found here: https://youtu.be/wRWCK9zGynA
Also, in a funny twist the Foundation winds up getting the tip on where to find Roland's killer from the UIU of all places, as in the song it is stated that Roland's initial killing was ordered by the CIA.

Any and all feedback is greatly appreciated!

item.title: SCP Idea - Algernon-13
item.description: A distant star, when viewed, enhances the viewer's "attributes" based upon what they define themselves as
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-fi, Light horror

Elevator Pitch: A dim, distant star is discovered by a group of astronomers who discover that, when extensively gazed upon, said star can temporarily impart seemingly supernatural enhancements to the viewer. Said enhancements come at a price, however.

Central Narrative: A small research team in Argentina discovers a hitherto unknown star. The initial astronomer who extensively gazes at the star notes a small mote of light in the corner of his eye, though the light dissipates after several hours, since he chooses to ignore it. His partner, however, continues to be bothered by the light in the corner of her eye and keeps staring at it. Once she stares at it for an arbitrary amount of time, she suddenly seizes a marker and begins scribbling strange symbols on a whiteboard. This fit lasts for approximately thirteen hours before she collapses from exhaustion. When she reawakens, she realizes that her knowledge of mathematics and science has been dramatically reduced to roughly that of a first-grade level.

SCP is made aware of this development and has its own team investigate the star, which has been designated Algernon-13 (after the novel "Flowers for Algernon"). Numerous personnel undergo tests, including a former soldier (who experiences increased aggression and muscle growth), a linguist (who briefly becomes an onmiglot), and an artist (who paints gorgeous pictures unlike any she'd ever made before, and which offers some insight into the nature of the star), all of whom suffer severe degradation of their enhanced abilities (i.e. the soldier experiencing muscle atrophy) after thirteen hours have passed. It also becomes apparent that the star is attempting to communicate in some way, and the SCP would detail their efforts to figure out what the star wants.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook involves the mystery behind why the star induces "attribute enhancements" on its viewers. The mystery reaches its zenith with the pictures painted by the artist, as they give a nebulous picture of what's going on around the star, leaving one with as many new questions as answers.

Additional Notes: Not sure what to rate this anomaly - Euclid or Keter class. Suggestions would be helpful.

item.title: The Lightswitch
item.description: Just a simple lightswitch that turns YOU off and on. Probably.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror (?)

Page Layout (Optional): Brief SCP article with most content being in Addendum

Elevator Pitch: A lightswitch that, when flicked on, gives the user life and, when flicked off, takes the user’s life. Things get more interesting when living creatures turn it on and dead creatures turn it off.

Central Narrative: The SCP is simple enough; if you flick it off, it takes your consciousness, rendering you essentially dead/vegative. If someone forces your corpse/vegative body to flick it on again, you gain your consciousness back.

The Foundation recovers the SCP from a GOI (likely MC&D) after someone in the GOI unwittingly flicked it on while alive, causing the user to take the previous user’s consciousness and turn into a human with two minds, with two separate consciousnesses and all of it’s memories and skills. The GOI then used this to its own advantage, killing targets and employees with high levels of skill/competence/important memories and then adding them to some central source (becoming a sort of librarian/bookkeeper of minds). The bookkeeper is then interviewed by the Foundation, and is very resilient to giving up any information related to the GOI. Forcing a corpse to switch it off creates a “black hole” of consciousness, as the lightswitch attempts to drain the corpse of consciousness but finds nothing. The corpse then becomes SCP-XXXX-2, which constantly emits an aura of consciousness drain around it, slowly draining those within range of intelligence, reaction speed, emotional response and memories.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Keeping it short and simple, with an addendum explaining the GOI’s usage and recovery notes.

Additional Notes: I imagine the article itself will be brief (here is a lightswitch, it turns people on and off, no testing allowed, etc) with an addendum that holds the real meat of the SCP (recovery, interview).

In the interview, the Bookkeeper explains that he is the third iteration of them, and continuously absorbs the previous one before him. He mentions that plans were in place to try and create a sort of “generational immortality”, although they didn’t get very far.

The Foundation seriously considers having the captured Bookkeeper forcibly switching it off, then having one of their own agents/D-Class flick it on to take all the previous memories, however they get denied out of the fear that the new personalities may be overwhelming/resistant, and they would just end up back where they started, with another Bookkeeper that refuses to cooperate.

item.title: Just The Two Of Us
item.description: Basically it is a large humanoid entity accompanied by a feline in which it holds close whilst resorting to violence if it deems it necessary in order to protect it. Both carnivores that don't necessarily spare those below them but are happy to cooperate with those above.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Bits of Horror and Action.

Elevator Pitch: The basic idea is that a large humanoid creature is found accompanied with a feline in which they seemed to hold a link where the former guards the latter in an overprotective style.
This meaning that anything that draws close to the cat would be considered a potential threat if it was the first time encountering one another and multiple, timed sessions would need to be implemented before the human comes off its high guard.
Before containment this would be how the specimens got their food as the harmless looking cat would lure in people who stumbled into secluded areas only to be snatched up by the humanoid creature for a quick kill and feast during the early hours.
However both appear to harness a certain weakness to nature so wood, fruit or vegetables would render them either weakened or agitated depending on the dosage provided at that time making it a good counter measure during a containment breach if used properly.
The level of understanding held by both specimens could be exploited by persuading them into helping the facility when keeping other SCPs secured or when cross testing to give varying results due to how differently the two may react in different situations. The human helping to dispatch or beat back threats whilst the cat can provide comfort to those panicking as long as the two are kept relatively close to one another. It would require training and bargaining, though.

Central Narrative: The two would originally be found within a town after multiple disappearance are reported only for a task force to discover the hideout of the anomalies until they come to a conclusion that suits the both of them. After being well contained in their new home they seem relatively fine with their living arrangements but soon begin asking for more things in exchange for doing tasks or participating in cross testing procedures when being asked about it. This would lead to contained cross testing between different SCPs of the human's capabilities once in an enraged form after the cat is removed from the select distance previously set up with cross testing the cat with safe class human SCPs to see if progress can be made with them in any way. Conversation would spark up about how the humanoid's strength seemed to be enough to counter even keter class SCPs and potential to manipulate it into helping out task forces could be considered in upcoming missions.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The bond between the two being demonstrated only to be used by the foundation to create a weapon out of the humanoid creating a blackmail scenario where it tries to be with its cat once again whilst remaining within the rules it agreed to. Not to mention, the diverse between understanding and blind rage it has to swap constantly between if it doesn't want to risk being terminated by either the SCPs or the scientists that have it under lock and key. Meanwhile the cat sits inside the once lively containment cell awaiting its other half's return or plotting an escape by clawing into the wooden walls and being forced to further develop its anomalous abilities such as the bell being shaken more to amplify the effects it currently has. All the while it isn't considered what might happen if one were to perish considering how close they both are even though they both subtly drop hints of great evil erupting from within the other if it were to happen.

item.title: Accessible Issue
item.description: I’m sure this seems stupid to old veterans, but Id like to be heard out
item.content:encoded:
Hello,

So the SCP Foundation is an incredible premise that can create some unique stories based on it’s premise alone. That being said, as someone who has now made multiple attempts at SCP’s I’d like to talk about some issues I see in the sight as an outsider.

+ Greenlight Troubles
- Greenlight Troubles

The site’s process for creating new SCPs, especially for new creators, is close focused at best. The fictional Foundation is supposed to be a clinical world facing fantastical elements, but as someone coming in, the similarities to the real site are a bit unnerving. To say nothing of the users, from personal experience they are fine, and sometimes friendly, this is purely about how a brand new author. To give credit, yes an author can develop ideas outside the site plenty, but that doesn't change they then have to convince at least two reviewers in a small paragraph there idea is worth it. Not impossible, obviously, but a little convoluted. I think the ability for more freedom in trying to convey what makes an idea worth it could benefit this site greatly. Once again: this spot isn’t impossible, but cam present real problems to someone in trying to cram an idea into a small format.

+ Aaaand its gone
- Aaaand its gone

The rating system means with -10 likes, a page meets the criteria for deletion. Now again, I can appreciate the benefits of running a strict site, but something about this seems a little cruel. For a site requiring hard work from new creators, all it takes is ten people deciding to press a button saying they didn’t like it, and that says to the author this page is worthy of deletion. It could be absolutely certain that if every site had a shallow enough criteria, many beloved posts would be gone before they blew up. Im not saying enough downvotes isn’t indicative of a post possibly needing deletion, but maybe that particular field needs to be stretched, and authors in general given a chance. After all theres no way to actually know if the majority of site users dislike an SCP, the votes are only indicative of the people who found that page.

+ Slightly Personal
- slightly personal

Once again, I’m sure to some this seems like the ravings of a writer who was a little hurt, and in some part I give credit that it does come from that. More so though, I’d argue that this is also the perspective of someone who has worked hard to try and join really creative people, and been turned away not necessarily by them, but by a system coming across as super insular. It occurs to me maybe I’m also ridiculous for trying to join a catalogue cresting the 6000’s, but under the impression that this universe could be even more I did wanna try. Definitely some fault is mine in writing, lets not pretend any old SCP’s I made would be the next 096, but my point lies in that: in trying to add to something I’ve seen as fun and a little silly, I’ve been met with an incredibly high wall, in some ways earned by the site, but in many ways just as ridiculous.

In closing: the site’s a little too insular. This doesn’t necessarily warrant a whole overhaul, but maybe a reflective look at how some things should be run. I suppose if you want to write this off as a newbee venting, thats fine, but I think it would great benefit the Foundation to genuinely look at how it handles new ideas, and what kind of criteria it has, and whether or not its always fair.

item.title: Love at Long Last
item.description: Interdimensional communication allows husband and wife to say goodbye...and accidentally ruin the world.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): existential/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional):

  • Credentials Required
  • Object Description (yellow universe)
  • Object Description (red universe)
  • A series of messages between two Foundation personnel from parallel universes, (yellow universe)
  • A series of messages between two Foundation personnel from parallel universes (Red universe)
  • Event Log: Gothic Storm: First known RMK-Class Scenario for both parallel worlds (Yellow universe)
  • Event Log: Gothic Storm: First known RMK-Class Scenario for both parallel worlds (Red universe)

Elevator Pitch:

+ show block
– hide block


The object is a pair of particles in between two separate branching worlds that allow for the communication between these two timelines via the transmission of information (possibly through Morse Code). A researcher by the name of Dr. Underwood attempts to contact her recently-deceased husband's counterpart in the alternate timeline, in a world where she had died rather than him during a similar event (possibly a containment breach, as both had worked together at the foundation when alive). The article contains a record of these messages, as well as documentation of cataclysmic events that transpired as a result of Dr. Underwood's attempts to reconnect with her husband.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

Dr. Underwood's husband had recently died two years prior due to a freak accident. Underwood isolates herself to focus on her work, and makes a breakthrough in inter-dimensional communication, where she comes into contact with Dr. Chase, her husband's counterpart in another dimension. In their communication, Chase reveals that Underwood had been the one to pass in his dimension, rather than him. As they talk, massive differences between the two worlds become evident, the primary one being that Chase's universe orbits a Red Dwarf while Underwood's earth (our Earth) orbits a Yellow dwarf. Eventually, the two realize that their communication is causing their realities to bleed into one another. Chase attempts to sever their connection to keep the two worlds separate, but Underwood continues to message him. This causes both particles to combine, accelerate the fusion process between both worlds. This leads to an event known as "Gothic Storm", the first known Reality-Merging Class Scenario (RMK-Class) in that reality. The aftermath is chaotic, and leads to public awareness of the Foundation, the release of numerous anomalies, and shifts of entire galaxies in the universe. Dr. Underwood had seemingly disappeared, while Dr. Chase was discovered in her office. The document ends with an interview with Chase, and remains the only documentation of this event

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The concept of an RMK-Class Scenario hasn't been used much on the wiki before. Additionally, it (attempts to) question the ethics of sacrificing the whole for personal gain. It attempts to paint the characters as both selfish and stingy, as well as human and sympathetic. I will admit that the concept itself isn't the most original, but the story and its consequences certainly are.

Additional Notes: This isn't my original story: I received the idea from this youtube video, and tried to make a unique ending: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K3W61Ae0M9g

item.title: The Unrune (For Greenlight)
item.description: A bizarre rune that makes no sense and a man that makes even less
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP layout followed by information on where the object was recovered from and the groups connected with it. Possible addendums or test logs will tie in more of the important story

Elevator Pitch: A rune stone that defies physics, disobeys logic, and removes any sense of comfort. According to all attempts to gather data, it doesn't exist, yet we perceive it with our senses. However the rune engraved on it can only be seen, not felt, and in any image of the object it is blank.

Central Narrative: A cult worshipping the god of chaos believes this rune stone imprisons him and it is their duty to set him free once more. The GOC ended up with it, tried to destroy it and couldn't, and decided to give it to the foundation since containing is more their speed. The rune isn't what the cult thinks, but there's more to it than the foundation knows and it ties into a larger story relating to this so called god and his cult.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The object defies reality and physics and is tied to some god, but isn't really dangerous or powerful. It's more focused on the story I want to introduce but a reality defying object that doesn't do much and a god that isn't a god might be refreshing amongst the massive distortions and apocalyptic deities.

Additional Notes: This IS NOT meant to be some new all powerful, world ending, eldritch being. I don't want to make this about yet another god who wants to destroy humanity. I'm starting small, with this rune, so I don't come across like it's my goal to top anybody else or "have the baddest scp". Just want some cool ideas and a good story because that's what I personally love.

item.title: Worldwarden

item.content:encoded:

Elevator Pitch:

Narrative etc here
wow there it is

When the Foundation contains the subject and removes the parasite, the daughter returns to normal. (disclaimer: it is not lost on me that this is a sensitive topic. As a trans individual myself, it is my intention to play on the horror of a transphobic mother/daughter relationship, and not to merely act out conversion therapy.)

In the second, shortest log, a child in a healthy relationship with the mother is infected, but the parasite shrivels and dies, unable to increase its intake of affection because the mother is happy with her child as they are.

In the third, a parasite manifests in an extremely (but subtly) abusive relationship in which the mother exhibits masked hostility towards her child. The parasite, unable to find a form that would please the mother, mutates the host in bizarre ways before bringing them to the brink of death, implying that the only scenario that would please this mother is the near-death of her child. The Foundation recovers the parasite, resuscitates the victim, and re-homes them away from their mother.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A parasite that horrifies readers not only with biological manipulation, but also by visibly manifesting the toxic consequences of abusive expectations for adult children. item.title: SCP-5311
item.content:encoded:
The core idea here is definitely viable. Classic vanilla killer monsters are hard to pull off, but the anomaly is a good one to carry something like that. Ditch the targeting of people who know about it and the sound-trigger thing; this thing only needs the one party trick. It's a solid one.

I'm just going to do a rough breakdown here, if you take this to the forums for an overhaul and second try (and you should) PM me and I'll do a more in-depth one. I'm being a little blunt here because I think this is a strong idea but it will only work with a total overhaul.

The surface problems are tone breaks and bad formatting - scare italics in the Containment procedures, overdramatic statements of how dangerous it is, directly addressing the reader, hard-to-read paragraph organization… lots of little things that draft critique can help you address.

More than that though, you're totally missing the mark on what makes this thing a good monster, and how to present it. There's a lot here telling us we should be afraid of this thing, and not nearly enough showing us any of it. Tied into that, you also show your cards way, way too early, especially with regard to the strongest parts of this.

For instance, Don't beat us over the head with everything that qualifies as a pipe immediately in the containment procedures. Keep it subtle, just say it has to be kept x meters from tube-like structures or objects, and describe how it moves between pipes and manipulates the flow of things through them. And then let it click into place when the containment team points a gun at it. You can do the same with containment breaches demonstrating the endless series of things which can be considered tubes. There's potential for this thing to be scary as hell, it just needs to be used right.

The machine can also be used to harvest energy from any sentient life (on par with humans, but not animals).It comes attached with a tower-like battery with a vast storage capacity (it's built to contain the sum of a God's power) the size of a 2 story building.

Even though each individual human provides a lot of power (in terms of electricity), it takes the equivalent of a genocide of tragic proportions to fill the battery even an 1/8th of the way. It was 1/3 full as found.

Basically this is set sometime in the near future where the transition from Oil to energy is more complete. Oil is thus almost obselete, and cars and the like which used to run on oil have been adapted to use electricity.

In this setting, the Foundation finds that India has been utilising the machine to meet the vast energy demands of the country. Large solar power plants are already being built in real life in India for much the same reason.

The energy obtained from the machine is 'laundered' through the solar power plants.

The scheme was introduced as a stop gap till a better energy source could be developed, but then inertia took hold. Since not many people were aware of it at any given time, and it served the purpose well, successive govts. decided it was easier to keep using it than to develop entirely new costly energy sources.

The human input is secretly obtained from prisons, and occasionally political prisoners are used.

India in this setting becomes a major proponent of "clean" energy, since it has a way to produce a lot of it, and becomes a leading energy exporter, creating another incentive for the govt not to discontinue the program.

item.description: A small strand of ancient parasites that reek havoc on the body's digestive system and immune system.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Virus

Page Layout (Optional): Starts off with an ACS header, followed by a standard layout and descriptions and several test logs and incidents.

Elevator Pitch: What mysteries lie in the the ancient ice sheets of Antarctica? A new species of life? A city previously undiscovered? Or maybe a very rapid-spreading virus/parasite that is not matching to any discovered records and resistant to all antibodies?

Central Narrative: The pathogen is classified as EA-01 through EA-07. Each parasite has a classification of risk, ranging from A to F (A is safer, F is deadlier). The pathogen, discovered in lake Vostok, under the ancient Antarctica ice sheets, is unknown to man, is resistant to all antibodies, and is incurable by any means possible (including anomalous).

+ show block
– hide block

The path of destruction starts at the bladders, which contract the bladders, decreasing urine capacity. With the contraction comes frequent and painful urinating (6-10 times an hour). The filtering system within the bladders is also hijacked, so the "waste" disposed of in the urine gets sorted through into the body along with the minerals and vitamins. After two (2) days of exposure, the bladder will shrink to the size of a penny, allowing for no liquid to be stored, causing uncontrollable and excruciating urinating.

After the downfall of the urinary system, it attacks the immune system. It's main target is macrophages and B cells. Once the B cells fall to a critically low amount, it starts another attack on the immune system against the macrophages. They "bundle up" and start overwhelming the macrophages with such intense force that the guard cell just explodes. After the main targets are down, it feeds away at smaller cells, which help them grow in size. The parasites will then feast on blood rapidly, and cause mass blood clots, and stop blood flow almost entirely.

The subject exposed to Exil Apomus will either die from a variety of ways

  • blood loss
  • brain aneurysm
  • urinary tract infection
  • internal heart damage
  • another pathogen entering the weakened immune system
  • (very rare) Exil Apomus causes total organ failure, which results in inevitable death

Hook/Attention-Grabber: To be honest, if you like viruses and stuff like this, it would interest you. That's about it.

(if SCP-XXXX broadcasted to "channel 3," everyone tuned to "channel 3" would have their program interrupted by the alert, and by the alert's anomalous effects.)

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative:
When a small-town local news team, low on funds, had their broadcast station destroyed by a catastrophic weather event, they had to find some way to keep broadcasting. Luckily, someone very close to the town happened to own a broadcast station, and sold it to them dirt-cheap as an act of generosity. Once the news team was set up in the brand-new station (SCP-XXXX-1), they resumed their regular schedule, and got accustomed to the new workplace without incident. However, a few weeks/months later, a storm front was rolling in, and cyclones forming close to the town. They broadcasted the tornado warning alert, triggering an anomalous disaster in their town. The connection between the warning and the anomaly was not yet apparent.

They continued to use the warning messages in times that called for them, consistently triggering catastrophes in town. Eventually, the constant anomalous disasters in town devastated local businesses. With nobody paying for advertising, and the town's population facing a rapid decrease, the local news channel was no longer profitable, and was losing money. The news team fell into massive debt, and then fell apart.

The Foundation took notice of the town's high rate of anomalous events, and realized the cause when the news station's shutdown corresponded with complete cessation of anomalies.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The story of the town's downfall as a result of the station would be the most interesting part in my opinion.

The different anomalies caused by the broadcasts could also be potentially pretty interesting.

Additional Notes:
If it gets greenlit I'll definitely be doing a lot of research on how local news stations actually operate. If anyone has experience with local TV broadcasting, it would be good for me to have someone to consult about terminology and accuracy.
